name: Apple
description: Crisp and sweet-tart, apples are one of the most widely grown tree fruits in the world.
benefits: Skin carries most of the antioxidants

name: Banana
description: A soft, energy-dense fruit, popular as a quick source of natural sugars and potassium.

name: Orange
description: A juicy citrus fruit famous for its vitamin C content and refreshing acidity.
benefits: Hydrating due to high water content

name: Grapes
description: Small, juicy fruits that grow in clusters, eaten fresh or dried as raisins.
benefits: Rich in resveratrol from the skin

name: Mango
description: Known as the king of fruits in South Asia, mangoes are sweet, fragrant, and fiber-rich.
benefits: High in vitamin A and C

name: Strawberry
description: A bright red, seed-covered berry with a sweet flavor and very low calorie density.
benefits: More vitamin C by weight than oranges

name: Blueberry
description: Small round berries prized for their deep color and dense antioxidant content.

name: Pineapple
description: A tropical fruit with a spiky rind and juicy, tangy-sweet flesh.

name: Watermelon
description: A large melon that is over 90% water, making it one of the most hydrating fruits.

name: Papaya
description: A soft tropical fruit with orange flesh, valued for aiding digestion.

name: Guava
description: A fragrant fruit common across South Asia with an exceptionally high vitamin C content.
benefits: One of the richest fruit sources of vitamin C

name: Pomegranate
description: A fruit filled with juicy, ruby-red seeds (arils) known for strong antioxidant activity.

name: Kiwi
description: A fuzzy-skinned fruit with bright green flesh, tiny seeds, and a tangy-sweet taste.
benefits: More vitamin C by weight than oranges

name: Peach
description: A stone fruit with soft, fuzzy skin and sweet, fragrant flesh.

name: Plum
description: A small stone fruit with smooth skin, ranging from tart to sweet.

name: Pear
description: A sweet, grainy-textured fruit related to the apple, often eaten with the skin on.
benefits: Low allergenic risk, gentle on digestion

name: Cherry
description: Small, glossy stone fruits with a balance of sweetness and tartness.

name: Lychee
description: A small tropical fruit with a rough pink rind and sweet, floral white flesh.

name: Watermelon (yellow)
description: A yellow-fleshed watermelon variety, similarly hydrating with a slightly honeyed taste.

name: Avocado
description: A creamy, high-fat fruit botanically classed as a berry, with a mild nutty flavor.

name: Fig
description: A soft fruit with a mildly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture from tiny edible seeds.
benefits: Contains calcium, unusual for a fruit

name: Coconut
description: A fibrous tropical fruit with dense, fatty flesh, higher in calories than most fruit.

name: Grapefruit
description: A large, tangy citrus fruit that can be pink, red, or white-fleshed.
benefits: High in vitamin C and A

name: Lemon
description: A very sour citrus fruit, usually used for its juice and zest rather than eaten whole.
benefits: Low sugar for a citrus fruit

name: Raspberry
description: A delicate, hollow-cored berry with a distinctive tart-sweet flavor.
benefits: Exceptionally high fiber for a fruit

name: Blackberry
description: A dark, glossy aggregate berry with a deep, slightly tart flavor.
benefits: High in fiber and vitamin K

name: Dragon Fruit
description: A striking pink or yellow fruit with speckled white or red flesh and a mild sweetness.

name: Custard Apple
description: A sweet, creamy tropical fruit with segmented flesh and a custard-like texture.

name: Jackfruit
description: The largest tree-borne fruit, with sweet, fibrous pods often used as a meat substitute when unripe.

name: Apricot
description: A small, velvety-skinned stone fruit with a mildly sweet and tangy flavor.

name: Cantaloupe
description: A fragrant orange-fleshed melon with a netted rind, rich in vitamin A.
benefits: High in vitamin A and C

name: Sweet Lime (Mosambi)
description: A sweet, low-acid citrus fruit popular in South Asia, often consumed as juice.
benefits: Gentle on the stomach compared to sour citrus

name: Sapodilla (Chikoo)
description: A brown-skinned tropical fruit with a grainy, malty-sweet flesh similar to brown sugar.

name: Star Fruit
description: A crunchy, star-shaped-when-sliced fruit with a mild, slightly tart flavor.

name: Cranberry
description: A tart, firm berry rarely eaten raw, commonly dried, juiced, or used in sauces.

name: Muskmelon
description: A sweet, aromatic melon with pale green flesh, popular as a summer cooler in South Asia.

name: Potato
description: A starchy root vegetable, one of the most widely eaten staple foods in the world.
benefits: High in resistant starch when cooked and cooled

name: Tomato
description: Botanically a fruit but used as a vegetable, tomatoes are low-calorie and rich in lycopene.
benefits: High in lycopene, more bioavailable when cooked

name: Onion
description: A pungent bulb vegetable used as a base flavor in cooking worldwide.

name: Carrot
description: A crunchy orange root vegetable, one of the richest everyday sources of beta-carotene.

name: Spinach
description: A dark leafy green packed with iron, folate, and vitamin K relative to its calories.
benefits: Very high in vitamin K and folate
Rich in iron, though non-heme and less absorbable

name: Broccoli
description: A cruciferous vegetable valued for its vitamin C and sulfur-containing compounds.

name: Cauliflower
description: A mild, versatile cruciferous vegetable often used as a low-carb substitute for grains.
benefits: High vitamin C for a low-calorie food

name: Cucumber
description: A cooling, water-rich vegetable often eaten raw in salads.
benefits: One of the lowest calorie foods by weight
Contains small amounts of vitamin K

name: Bell Pepper
description: A crisp, sweet member of the pepper family, available in green, red, and yellow.
benefits: Good source of vitamin A, especially red varieties

name: Sweet Potato
description: A sweet, orange-fleshed root vegetable with a lower glycemic impact than white potato.
benefits: Lower glycemic index than white potato

name: Cabbage
description: A dense leafy cruciferous vegetable, eaten raw, cooked, or fermented.
benefits: Good source of vitamin C and K

name: Green Peas
description: A sweet, starchy legume eaten as a vegetable, higher in protein than most vegetables.

name: Almonds
description: A nutrient-dense tree nut, high in healthy fats, protein, and vitamin E.
benefits: Rich in vitamin E, an antioxidant

name: Cashews
description: A creamy, kidney-shaped nut, slightly lower in fiber than almonds but rich in minerals.
benefits: Good source of copper and magnesium

name: Walnuts
description: A brain-shaped nut notably high in plant-based omega-3 fatty acids.
benefits: One of the best plant sources of omega-3 (ALA)

name: Pistachios
description: A green-kernelled nut that's unusually high in potassium and protein for a nut.
benefits: Highest potassium of the common nuts
Lower calorie density than most nuts, per kernel count

name: Raisins
description: Dried grapes, concentrated in natural sugar and calories compared to fresh grapes.
benefits: Concentrated source of iron and potassium
Good source of boron for bone health

name: Dates
description: A very sweet dried fruit from the date palm, traditionally used to break fasts.
benefits: High in fiber despite the sugar content
Good source of potassium and magnesium

name: Dried Apricot
description: Sun-dried apricots, concentrated in beta-carotene, potassium, and natural sugar.
benefits: High fiber for a dried fruit

name: Dried Figs
description: Dried figs with a chewy texture and high calcium content, unusual among fruit.
benefits: Good source of calcium, rare for a fruit

name: Peanuts
description: Technically a legume, peanuts are one of the most affordable, protein-dense dry fruits.
benefits: Highest protein of common nuts/legumes by weight

name: Pine Nuts
description: Small, soft seeds from pine cones, with a buttery flavor and the highest fat content among common nuts.
benefits: Contains pinolenic acid, linked to appetite regulation

name: Chicken Breast
description: A lean, high-protein poultry cut, one of the most common protein sources worldwide.
benefits: Low in saturated fat compared to red meat
Good source of B vitamins (niacin, B6)

name: Chicken Thigh
description: A darker, fattier poultry cut than breast meat, with a richer flavor.
benefits: Higher fat content keeps it moist when cooked

name: Mutton (Lamb)
description: A flavorful red meat from sheep, commonly used in South Asian curries and roasts.
benefits: High in heme iron, well absorbed
Good source of vitamin B12 and zinc

name: Beef (Lean)
description: A dense, iron-rich red meat, with fat content varying widely by cut.
benefits: Complete protein with all essential amino acids

name: Pork (Lean)
description: A versatile meat that ranges from lean (loin) to fatty (belly) depending on cut.
benefits: High in thiamine (vitamin B1), unusual among meats

name: Salmon
description: An oily fish prized for its high omega-3 fatty acid content.
benefits: Among the best sources of omega-3 (EPA/DHA)

name: Rohu Fish
description: A popular South Asian freshwater fish, lean and mild-flavored.

name: Egg
description: A complete, affordable protein source eaten boiled, fried, or scrambled.
benefits: Complete protein with all essential amino acids

name: Shrimp (Prawn)
description: A low-fat shellfish that's very high in protein relative to its calories.

name: Turkey Breast
description: An extra-lean poultry option, slightly leaner than chicken breast.

name: Potato Chips
description: Thin, deep-fried potato slices, salty and high in fat and sodium.
benefits: Occasional source of potassium from potato
Best enjoyed in moderation given fat and sodium

name: Popcorn (Air-popped)
description: A whole-grain snack that's light per cup when air-popped without added oil or butter.
benefits: Whole grain, high in fiber per calorie
Lower calorie density than fried snacks

name: Samosa
description: A deep-fried South Asian pastry, typically filled with spiced potatoes or minced meat.
benefits: Satisfying snack with carbs and fat for energy
Best balanced with vegetables or salad
High in sodium and fat — moderate portions recommended

name: Digestive Biscuit
description: A semi-sweet baked biscuit made with wholemeal flour, often eaten with tea.

name: Peanut Butter
description: A creamy spread made from ground peanuts, calorie-dense but protein-rich.
benefits: High protein and healthy fat content
Good source of niacin and magnesium

name: Granola Bar
description: A compact bar of oats, nuts, and sweeteners, marketed as a convenient energy snack.
benefits: Sugar content varies a lot by brand — check labels

name: Dark Chocolate (70%)
description: Chocolate with a high cocoa percentage, richer in antioxidants than milk chocolate.
benefits: Lower sugar than milk chocolate, still calorie-dense

name: Trail Mix
description: A mix of nuts, seeds, and dried fruit, built for portable, long-lasting energy.
benefits: Combines protein, fat, and quick-energy carbs
Good source of magnesium and potassium
Dried fruit adds sugar — portion matters

name: Roasted Chana (Chickpeas)
description: Dry-roasted chickpeas, a crunchy, high-protein, high-fiber snack popular across South Asia.
benefits: High protein and fiber for a snack
Low fat compared to fried snacks

name: Namkeen (Bhujia)
description: A deep-fried, spiced gram-flour snack mix, widely eaten across India.
benefits: Contains protein and fiber from gram flour
High in fat and sodium from frying and seasoning
Best in small portions as a side snack

name: Cheeseburger
description: A grilled beef patty with cheese in a bun, a staple of fast-food menus worldwide.
benefits: Provides protein and carbs in one item
High in saturated fat and sodium
Best balanced with a side salad instead of fries

name: Pizza (Cheese, 1 slice)
description: A wedge of cheese pizza — baked dough, tomato sauce, and melted cheese.
benefits: Provides carbs, protein, and calcium from cheese
Sodium and fat content add up fast over multiple slices
Topping choice (veg vs meat) changes the nutrition profile a lot

name: French Fries
description: Deep-fried potato strips, one of the most common fast-food sides.
benefits: High in fat from deep frying
Calorie-dense — easy to underestimate portion size

name: Fried Chicken (Piece)
description: Chicken coated in a seasoned batter and deep-fried, a global fast-food staple.
benefits: High in protein from the chicken itself
Batter and frying add significant fat and calories
Removing the skin/batter lowers calories substantially

name: Hot Dog
description: A grilled or boiled sausage served in a sliced bun, often with condiments.
benefits: Quick source of protein and carbs
Processed meat is high in sodium and saturated fat
Best as an occasional food, not a daily staple

name: Tacos (Beef, 2)
description: Folded tortillas filled with seasoned meat, cheese, and vegetables.
benefits: Balances protein, carbs, and some vegetables
Toppings (lettuce, tomato, salsa) add fiber and vitamins
Cheese and sour cream add saturated fat quickly

name: Instant Noodles
description: Pre-cooked, dried noodle blocks with a seasoning packet, ready in minutes.
benefits: Very high in sodium per serving
Adding an egg or vegetables improves the nutrition balance

name: Creamy Pasta
description: Pasta tossed in a rich cream or cheese-based sauce.
benefits: Provides carbs and some protein from cheese/cream
High in saturated fat from the cream sauce
A tomato-based sauce swap cuts calories substantially

name: Club Sandwich
description: A layered sandwich with turkey or chicken, bacon, lettuce, tomato, and mayo.
benefits: Good protein content from the meat layers
Bacon and mayo add significant saturated fat
Lettuce and tomato contribute some fiber and vitamin C

name: Donut (Glazed)
description: A deep-fried, sugar-glazed dough ring, a popular sweet breakfast or snack item.
benefits: Quick source of energy from sugar and fat
Very little fiber, vitamins, or minerals
Best treated as an occasional treat
